prompts.name: 01-mvc-meaning-v1
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / scientific-educational.
Create a single polished Korean educational web service UI image, portrait 1536x2048, for "javaExperience". This is a real high-fidelity image mockup of a readable learning page, not code and not a generic slide or infographic collage. Intent: a beginner reads it like a calm illustrated story, eventually able to reason at professional backend depth. Use a light warm-white reading surface, ink-navy typography, precise restrained blue/teal/amber semantic accents, generous space, refined editorial Korean sans typography, beautifully crafted vectorlike visual objects and thin connection lines. Professional quiet product design, not childish mascots, not flashy gradients, not marketing. Consistent small top nav "javaExperience   배우기   시나리오   실습". Small left progress rail and a wide main reading column. Most of the image is the teaching content, not navigation.
CRITICAL: Each concept explanation is visible as short narrative + a purpose-built explanatory visual; NO accordions or stacks of collapsed cards. Alternate text and visuals in a deliberate reading sequence. Use only the short exact Korean copy requested below and English identifiers; do not invent long paragraphs or microtext. Clearly readable at full resolution. Controls are mock UI, no fake live telemetry or completion badges. Footer label "화면 시안 · 설명용 예시". Aim to show how prose becomes understandable visual explanation.
Topic: WHAT MVC MEANS, BEFORE discussing service/repository layers.
Title exactly "MVC는 무엇을 나누는 걸까요?"
Intro exactly "같은 게시글도, 데이터와 보이는 모습과 사용자 행동은 다릅니다."
Central hero: an actual beautifully composed mini 게시글 detail UI with title "첫 글", author "김자바", and a "수정" button. Three aligned explanatory callouts pull distinct aspects from this ONE scene with clearly traced connections:
"Model" / "게시글의 데이터와 규칙" connected to an object document { title: "첫 글" };
"View" / "사용자에게 보이는 모습" connected to the rendered article;
"Controller" / "사용자의 요청을 처리하는 연결점" connected to the edit action.
This is a conceptual relationship scene, not Model -> View -> Controller pipeline.
Next section title "제목을 바꾸면 무엇이 달라질까요?"
Two side-by-side small frames with a common blue title-field highlight: "첫 글" then "수정한 글"; connect data change and updated rendered title. Caption "데이터가 바뀌면, 화면은 그 결과를 보여줍니다."
Next section "Spring에서는 응답 방식도 선택합니다."
Two clearly separate small branches: "HTML 화면" with labels "Model + View" -> browser page; "JSON API" with labels "응답 DTO" -> "HttpMessageConverter" -> JSON "{ \"title\": \"첫 글\" }". Caption "JSON 응답은 서버의 View 렌더링을 거치지 않습니다."
Important visible separate comparison strip "MVC와 계층형 구조는 보는 관점이 다릅니다." followed by "Controller · Service · Repository" and tiny descriptor "웹 요청 · 업무 규칙 · 저장소 접근"; make NOT one-to-one equality to Model View Controller. No database-as-Model claim. No View-as-Service.
Bottom small prediction question "같은 데이터를 다른 화면으로 보여주면, 무엇을 바꾸면 될까요?" plus simple answer choice buttons "View" "Repository". Do not reveal correct answer via styling.

Use a light warm-white reading surface, ink-navy typography, precise restrained blue/teal/amber semantic accents, generous space, refined editorial Korean sans typography, beautifully crafted vectorlike visual objects and thin connection lines. Professional quiet product design, not childish mascots, not flashy gradients, not marketing. Consistent small top nav "javaExperience   배우기   시나리오   실습". Small left progress rail and a wide main reading column. Most of the image is the teaching content, not navigation.
CRITICAL: Each concept explanation is visible as short narrative + a purpose-built explanatory visual; NO accordions or stacks of collapsed cards. Alternate text and visuals in a deliberate reading sequence. Use only the short exact Korean copy requested below and English identifiers; do not invent long paragraphs or microtext. Clearly readable at full resolution. Controls are mock UI, no fake live telemetry or completion badges. Footer label "화면 시안 · 설명용 예시". Aim to show how prose becomes understandable visual explanation.
Topic: turn dense API prose into a visible request-and-response story.
Title exactly "저장을 눌렀는데, 아직 저장되지 않았어요"
Intro "첫 단계에서는 요청을 받고 success로 답하는 것까지만 만듭니다."
This corresponds specifically to scenario 1-1: no Service/Repository/database write in this lesson. Make a beautifully readable 4-scene sequential storyboard DOWN the page with the same title data value "첫 글" in consistent blue throughout. It is a learning page, not a dashboard.
Scene 1 "01  저장 버튼을 눌렀어요": mini real 글쓰기 form, 제목 field "첫 글", blue "저장" button. Short caption "입력한 값을 서버에 보냅니다."
Scene 2 "02  글자가 JSON이 되었어요": outgoing request paper/card "POST /api/posts", "Content-Type: application/json", body fragment '{ "title": "첫 글" }' with a visible "본문 일부" label. A small envelope moves across a network boundary toward a server shape. No claim JSON is object itself.
Scene 3 "03  서버에서 Java 객체로 읽었어요": distinguish two connected visual items "HttpMessageConverter" -> "PostCreateRequest", the DTO as a three dimensional flat document holding 'title = "첫 글"', then "PostController". Short caption "Spring이 JSON을 읽어 요청 객체를 만들고 Controller에 전달합니다." One unobtrusive "내부 흐름" note "DispatcherServlet → HandlerAdapter → 요청 본문 변환 → Controller". Do not confuse bean injection with JSON conversion.
Scene 4 "04  success가 돌아왔어요": incoming response card "200 OK" / "success", and original mini UI with toast "요청을 받았어요". Beside it a distinct neutral database cylinder and text "DB 저장 없음". Caption "응답 성공과 데이터 저장은 같은 뜻이 아닙니다."
Bottom knowledge check "서버를 다시 켜도 글이 남아 있을까요?" choice buttons "아니요" "네" equal styling; small next episode hint "다음 장면: 응답에 데이터 담기".
No finished-save checkmark. No SQL, no imaginary persisted id. Not a 7-column architecture diagram. Wide spacious sequential frames with only active stage large, a slim progress track ties the sequence together.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / scientific-educational.
Create a single polished Korean educational web service UI image, portrait 1536x2048, for "javaExperience". This is a real high-fidelity image mockup of a readable learning page, not code and not a generic slide or infographic collage. Intent: a beginner reads it like a calm illustrated story, eventually able to reason at professional backend depth. Use a light warm-white reading surface, ink-navy typography, precise restrained blue/teal/amber semantic accents, generous space, refined editorial Korean sans typography, beautifully crafted vectorlike visual objects and thin connection lines. Professional quiet product design, not childish mascots, not flashy gradients, not marketing. Consistent small top nav "javaExperience   배우기   시나리오   실습". Small left progress rail and a wide main reading column. Most of the image is the teaching content, not navigation.
CRITICAL: Each concept explanation is visible as short narrative + a purpose-built explanatory visual; NO accordions or stacks of collapsed cards. Alternate text and visuals in a deliberate reading sequence. Use only the short exact Korean copy requested below and English identifiers; do not invent long paragraphs or microtext. Clearly readable at full resolution. Controls are mock UI, no fake live telemetry or completion badges. Footer label "화면 시안 · 설명용 예시". Aim to show how prose becomes understandable visual explanation.
Topic: S09 JPA memory state versus database state. Use a comparison instrument, distinctly different from a pipeline or generic storyboard.
Title "제목을 바꿨는데, DB는 왜 그대로일까요?"
Intro "같은 게시글 42번을 서로 다른 자리에서 관찰합니다."
Hero: large three-column observatory with header "Java 객체", "앱 트랜잭션 안의 DB", "별도 연결의 새 조회". First row small scenario note "setter 호출 직후". Clearly show Java value title="수정한 글" highlighted amber, app DB title="첫 글" neutral, observer title="첫 글" neutral. A tiny snapshot card under Java "변경 전 스냅샷: 첫 글".
Below hero a five-position playback-style stepper, labels "조회" "객체 변경" "flush" then a fork into "commit" and "rollback", NOT sequential commit then rollback.
Main second scene header "flush: SQL이 실행돼요". Sample query shown legibly "UPDATE post SET title = '수정한 글' WHERE id = 42". State comparison now shows Java "수정한 글", app DB "수정한 글" / badge "미확정", separate new connection "첫 글". Caption "SQL 실행과 저장 확정은 다른 순간입니다."
Third scene a visually unmistakable fork, equal-size panels:
"commit" -> "별도 연결: 수정한 글"
"rollback" -> "별도 연결: 첫 글".
A side observation symbol for DBeaver located OUTSIDE the Java application boundary and directly observing MySQL, not on a Java processing pipeline.
Small readable assumption "기존 행 UPDATE 예시 · 별도 연결은 새 autocommit SELECT".
Bottom caveat in one elegant visible sentence "열려 있던 트랜잭션의 조회 결과는 격리 수준에 따라 달라질 수 있어요."
Final question "flush 뒤 예외가 나면, 제목은 확정됐을까요?" two equal options "아직 아니요" "이미 확정됐어요".
No unsupported persist INSERT timing, no wrong managed state after rollback statement, no live measurement claims.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / scientific-educational.
Create a single polished Korean educational web service UI image, portrait 1536x2048, for "javaExperience". This is a real high-fidelity image mockup of a readable learning page, not code and not a generic slide or infographic collage. Small left progress rail and a wide main reading column. Most of the image is the teaching content, not navigation.
CRITICAL: Each concept explanation is visible as short narrative + a purpose-built explanatory visual; NO accordions or stacks of collapsed cards. Alternate text and visuals in a deliberate reading sequence. Use only the short exact Korean copy requested below and English identifiers; do not invent long paragraphs or microtext. Clearly readable at full resolution. Controls are mock UI, no fake live telemetry or completion badges. Footer label "화면 시안 · 설명용 예시". Aim to show how prose becomes understandable visual explanation.
Topic: lost update in like counts, two requests with chronological interleaving. Distinct visual grammar: parallel time lanes, shared state, then before/after mechanism comparison.
Title "두 명이 눌렀는데, 왜 하나만 늘었을까요?"
Intro "서로 다른 두 사용자가 같은 순간에 좋아요를 눌렀어요."
At top tiny actual post card "첫 글" with heart count "5". Small "설명용 초기값" label.
Main large hero visual is a precisely legible vertical time diagram, time travels DOWN with explicit arrow "시간". Three lanes "요청 A" in blue, "DB" in neutral navy, "요청 B" in teal.
Four chronological rows:
t1: A "5 읽기", DB "5".
t2: B "5 읽기", DB "5".
t3: A "6 저장", DB changes to "6".
t4: B "6 저장", DB remains "6", with a subtle amber annotation "앞선 값을 덮어썼어요".
A and B each have a small local note "5 + 1 = 6". Do not imply second request reads 6.
At bottom of hero compare two large counters "기대 7" vs "결과 6". Short explanation "각자 읽은 값에 1을 더해서, 같은 6을 저장했어요."
Next visible section "더하기를 DB에서 한 번에 하면?"
One short code strip "UPDATE post SET like_count = like_count + 1 WHERE id = 16".
Below a contrasting shared-row timeline with value progression "5 → 6 → 7" and labels "요청 A" then "요청 B", explicitly showing serialization of row updates. Caption "각 UPDATE가 DB의 현재 값에 1을 더합니다."
Visible deeper question strip, not collapsed: "같은 사람이 두 번 눌렀다면?" with two identical user badges and a unique-pair key label "(post_id, member_id)". Text "중복 방지와 숫자 증가를 함께 설계해야 해요."
Footer technical boundary "원자 UPDATE만으로 전체 좋아요 기능이 완성되지는 않습니다. 트랜잭션·중복·교착 재시도도 확인합니다."
No claim increment-alone solves idempotency, no timing benchmark, no badge that tests already pass.
